judged_text: packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:10 — `body: new URLSearchParams({ calcomUserId: userId.toString(), appSlug, })` makes all refreshes for a user's multiple accounts on one provider indistinguishable to the parent application, so adding a second connected account requires changing the sync contract to identify the account; the strongest rebuttal is that self-hosters synchronize only one account per provider, but neither this contract nor the existing unconditional Google callback credential creation enforces that limitation, leaving supported multiple-account installations unrepresentable.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real architectural limitation in the new credential sync feature. Looking at refreshOAuthTokens.ts lines 6-13, the sync endpoint is called with only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` as identifiers. This means if a user has multiple accounts connected for the same app (e.g., two Google calendars), the parent application cannot distinguish between them. This is a legitimate design concern for the new feature, though it may be intentional for the initial implementation scope. The finding correctly notes this is a contract/architecture issue rather than a bug.
